canonical.name: A splitting p-modular system and OG-lattices are fixed before any reduction or block-theoretic comparison begins.
Finite-dimensional algebra radicals, module radicals, and finite-dimensional Nakayama supply the replacement for Maschke's semisimple route.
Projective covers exist, are unique up to isomorphism over the target, and identify indecomposable projectives by their simple heads.
For finite p-groups, the group algebra is local and therefore has only the trivial simple module in characteristic p.
Restriction and induction preserve projectives, Higman's trace criterion detects relative projectivity, and vertices and sources organize indecomposable modules.

canonical.name: Pro-p groups are the profinite groups built from finite p-group quotients, and the pro-p completion specializes the ordinary profinite completion to those quotients.
Zp is defined as compatible residue classes, carries the inverse-limit topology, and that topology is exactly the p-adic metric topology.
The integers map injectively and densely into Zp, which is therefore the pro-p completion of Z and sits inside the full profinite completion decomposition.
For finitely generated pro-p groups, the Frattini subgroup is the closure of [G,G]G^p and the topological Burnside basis theorem detects generation modulo Phi(G).
